paper.title: On Generation in Metric Spaces
paper.summary: Extends language generation to separable metric spaces using scale-sensitive novelty and closure dimension, characterizes uniform and non-uniform generation, studies doubling-space invariance and metric dependence, and relates the metric framework to earlier discrete generation.

formalization_scope.summary: Complete for the eighteen-item semantic inventory of arXiv v2: all nine main theorems, three corollaries, Proposition D.1, and Examples 4.5, 4.8, 4.9, 4.11, and B.3 are kernel-checked. Lemmas 2.1, C.1, and C.2 and the orthogonal covering estimate are also proved. Implementation, oracle execution, and complexity remain outside scope.
specializations: Closed-neighborhood membership uses the order characterization of an infimum bound, including the empty-set convention.

The distance is usually an explicit real-valued kernel. Theorems expose only the metric laws actually used and generally do not need the source separability assumption. Generator existence uses a nonempty ambient type.
Finite internal closure dimension is represented by a natural-number bound on witnesses, while finite-sample covering numbers still allow ambient centers.
UUS is separate from the raw generation predicates; the SemanticBoundary module proves that v2 UUS supplies threshold reachability and hence limit correctness at admissible scales.
Theorem 3.5 uses a real-line target-valued diagonal for every allowed scale pair; no P10 transport is used.
Theorem 4.4 encodes bi-Lipschitz equivalence by two positive global domination constants. Doubling is assumed only for the first metric and derived for the second.

The Proposition D.1 overview exposes the three generation equivalences for the discrete metric at independent scales in [0,1), without countability or UUS assumptions. The UUS/infinite-support equivalence remains available separately as discrete_uus_iff.
The formalization is deterministic, semantic, and classical; no extracted implementation or runtime bound is claimed.
Example 4.8 uses infinite positive index sets as in the source. Natural exponents include zero; the diagonal construction observes the resulting common g_3 point initially.

Example 4.11 uses zero-based dyadic layers, a genuine induced weighted Hilbert metric, equality of the induced topologies, and global bi-Lipschitz constants 1 and 2. Uniform generation uses the semantic common-core choice generator.
gaps: Appendix A recalls earlier results and has no new P21 headline wrappers; Appendix E oracle/computability discussion is outside the semantic scope.
No independent human source-correspondence audit is claimed.

claims.statement_summary: Uniform generation at two novelty scales is characterized by finite scale-closure dimension for a uniformly unbounded-support class.

source_assessment.notes: This entry assesses the revised v2 statement. Both directions of the uniform-generation characterization use the revised internal-cover closure dimension. No extra internalization premise is imposed.

claims.title: Finite and countable metric classes are generatable at ordered scales
claims.statement_summary: Finite UUS classes are uniformly generatable and countable UUS classes are non-uniformly generatable when the generator novelty scale does not exceed the adversary scale.

source_assessment.notes: This entry assesses the revised v2 statement. Finite and countable class conclusions retain the revised UUS and ordered positive scale hypotheses. Finite upper bounds and intersected enumeration prefixes handle degenerate countable classes.

formalization.notes: The overview generalizes Corollaries 3.2 and 3.4 to a nonempty ambient type, reflexivity, nonnegative adversary scale, and ordered scales, without UUS or upper bounds by r. Finite upper bounds and intersected enumeration prefixes handle degenerate countable classes.

claims.title: Failure of finite-union closure on the real line
claims.statement_summary: For every allowed scale pair, two uniformly generatable r-UUS classes on the real line have a union that is not generatable in the limit.

source_assessment.notes: This entry assesses the revised v2 statement. For each r > 0 and 0 < adversary and generator scales <= r, two real-line r-UUS classes are uniformly generatable, but their union is not limit-generatable. The diagonal stays in both fixed targets and covers both.

claims.title: Generation invariance under bi-Lipschitz equivalent metrics
claims.statement_summary: If the first metric is doubling and the second is bi-Lipschitz equivalent, UUS, uniform generation, and non-uniform generation are invariant between the metrics.

source_assessment.notes: This entry assesses the revised v2 statement. The v2 bi-Lipschitz invariance theorem is proved. Only the first metric is assumed doubling; doubling of the second is derived. The raw generation equivalences hold without an additional UUS premise.

claims.title: Monotonicity in adversary and generator novelty scales
claims.statement_summary: Limit generation is preserved when both scales decrease, while uniform and non-uniform generation are preserved when the adversary scale increases and the generator scale decreases.

source_assessment.notes: This entry assesses the revised v2 statement. All three monotonicity clauses are proved by reusing the same generator; the abstract proofs need only scale inequalities.

formalization.notes: All three monotonicity clauses are proved by reusing the same generator; the abstract proofs need only scale inequalities. The Theorem 4.7 overview presents the uniform and non-uniform implications together, with each independently usable.

claims.title: Generation transfer under one-sided metric domination
claims.statement_summary: If one metric is bounded above by a positive multiple of another, UUS and generation in the limit transfer with the corresponding inverse scale change.

source_assessment.notes: This entry assesses the revised v2 statement. Both revised UUS and generation in the limit transfer under one-sided metric domination with the exact rescaled radii.

formalization.notes: UUS and generation in the limit transfer independently under one-sided metric domination with the exact rescaled radii. The overview packages two implications: UUS transfer requires source UUS, while generation transfer requires source generation, in addition to the shared positive domination constant and distance bound.

claims.title: The discrete metric recovers the earlier generation framework
claims.statement_summary: For the zero-one discrete metric and scales below one, metric limit, uniform, and non-uniform generation coincide with the earlier countable-space notions.

source_assessment.notes: This entry assesses the revised v2 statement. The revised UUS condition is exactly infinite support under the discrete metric. The limit, uniform, and non-uniform predicates reduce to P02 semantics at scales below one.

formalization.notes: The overview packages the limit, uniform, and non-uniform generation equivalences in proposition_D_1 at independent scales epsilon and epsilon-prime in [0,1), without countability or UUS assumptions. The auxiliary UUS/infinite-support equivalence from the source proof remains separately available as discrete_uus_iff in DiscreteReduction.lean.

lean_links.notes: The overview exposes only the three generation equivalences at independent scales epsilon and epsilon-prime in [0,1), generalizing the source countable domain and omitting its UUS assumption. The discrete UUS/infinite-support helper discrete_uus_iff remains available separately; the overview has no radius r parameter.
